Apple has removed a billboard in Milan that depicted a young child holding an iPhone, as part of its latest "Relax, it's iPhone" advertising campaign. Details below.

Apple Removes Controversial Italian Billboard

A few days ago, Italy's child welfare watchdog, the Autorità Garante per l'Infanzia e l'Adolescenza (AGIA), condemned Apple over imagery in its "Relax, it's iPhone" campaign showing a young child holding an iPhone.

The ad campaign focuses on the device's durability and ruggedness, showing iPhones being dirtied, dropped, or used in ways that might damage them — including someone taking photos in a heavy downpour, someone watching videos on the edge of a bathtub, a dog biting an iPhone, and a young child clumsily holding the device.

After a billboard depicting this last scenario was erected in Milan's via Melchiorre Gioia, AGIA received a letter from a member of the public stating that the ad normalises "digital babysitting".

AGIA agreed with this view and referred the case to Italy's communications regulator AGCOM, the Italian Competition Authority AGCM, and the country's advertising industry self-regulatory organisation IAP, "for appropriate scrutiny and any action."

Now, according to Prima Comunicazione and Repubblica Milano, Apple has removed the controversial billboard and replaced it with one promoting the device's "Find My" feature.

Apple has yet to publicly respond to the incident, but the company's swift action reflects how seriously it takes such criticism, even when an ad intended to convey iPhone's durability has been interpreted differently by the public.
